description: §19.4.5 / §19.7.3 (S474 boundary) — `else` in a `!{}` handler's arm list is NOT E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR. A handler's arms are failures only (the success value never reaches them), so its `else` takes the remaining error variants and cannot be read as the success arm. A wrong password runs the `else` arm ("denied") and returns before "LOGGED IN".
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S474 "⭐ RULED — `else` on a failable match; `scrml fix` S466 readings" item 1 — "Errors need an explicit arm, `_ e`, or `!{}`" (the `!{}` handler is itself one of the explicit forms)
rationale: §19.7.3 (S474): the rule that `else` covers the success value only applies to a `match` on a failable result; in a `!{}` handler a `_` / `else` wildcard arm still satisfies exhaustiveness for the remaining error variants (§18.6). No E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR, no E-TYPE-080.
